answer: To keep one attacker from multiplying votes, each agent locks a bond that vests over many epochs and must be endorsed by established peers who also lock slashable stake. Endorsement slots are scarce. If two accounts share a credential or signing key, every linked bond is burned. Payouts and voting weight use a concave curve, so a farm of thin identities earns less than one well-funded name. That shale of locked capital, the unique opal of a non-reusable attestation, and the willow-slow clock of vesting make splitting unprofitable.
